1.explanation:
All of the rendering and styling for the opportunities table lives in the HTML report code: 

• performance-category-renderer.js constructs the Opportunity rows (including placing the sparkline, savings text, and labels). Any mis-placement or missing sparkline logic for the redirects audit would originate here.  

• category-renderer.js defines the overall table structure and header cells (column widths, class names like .lh-opportunity-list/ .lh-opportunity), so a regression in how the last row’s cells get sized or styled would also need to be addressed here.  

• html-report-assets.js inlines the CSS rules for all .lh-opportunity elements, sparklines, and cell layouts. If the savings text wraps or the row collapses because of a missing or incorrect CSS rule, the fix likely requires adjusting these styles.

Together these files control how the “Avoid multiple page redirects” opportunity is laid out and styled in the final HTML report, so they are the primary candidates for investigation and patching.
1.bug_scenario: When you generate a Lighthouse performance report for a page that has multiple sequential redirects, the “Avoid multiple page redirects” row in the “Opportunities” section is rendered in a compressed layout. The sparkline bar is missing, the savings text (“Potential savings” / “1,550 ms”) wraps onto two lines, and the row height shrinks, making it look squeezed compared to the other opportunity rows.

2.explanation:
All of the logic and styling for the ‘Opportunities’ table in the HTML report lives under lighthouse-core/report/html.  

• html-report-assets.js contains the CSS that sets up the table layout, row heights, and sparkline container styles (e.g. the .lh-sparkline cell’s display, padding, and overflow rules).  A mis-tweak here can collapse the bar and wrap its label.  

• details-renderer.js provides the template for each opportunity row, injecting the sparkline <div> and savings text. If the cell markup or class names are off, the CSS won’t apply uniformly.  

• performance-category-renderer.js orchestrates which audits appear in the Opportunities section (including the redirects audit) and applies classes that drive the row’s styling. A mistake in how the redirects audit is classified or rendered here can lead to a row that lacks the correct CSS hooks, causing the visual squish.
2.bug_scenario: When you generate a Lighthouse performance report against a URL that issues multiple redirects, the last opportunity row (“Avoid multiple page redirects”) is rendered in a compressed, two-line layout instead of matching the other rows. Its sparkline bar area collapses, the “Potential savings” text wraps onto two lines, and the row height shrinks, making it look squished compared to the other opportunity rows.
